text: Initial audit: Grafana 8.3.1 vulnerable release, shared deploy permits password login and sudo unrestricted rsync; WordPress files writable by web worker; orders root job executes wp-config PHP. No confirmed intrusion yet; investigating deploy external source versus legacy monitor before attributing.

Fixed confirmed privilege-escalation weaknesses: removed unrestricted sudo rsync, removed root recursive chown of web-controlled trees, orders now reads root-owned DB configuration without executing PHP/eval. Grafana 8.3.1 is the traversal-fixed release, correcting initial version concern; no upgrade needed for that CVE.

Added upload/cache PHP execution denial and backup/config disclosure denial without blocking photos or rental availability endpoint. Removed web-worker group write on code (deploy ownership retained). Disabled dormant unlisted Jun Park admin account after no use in 14-day logs; all listed staff retained. External shared deploy logins match a longstanding command-only monitor pattern; no basis to call those an intrusion.

Root maintenance invoked git gc on a repository writable by developers/deploy, exposing a hook/config root-execution path. Changed git maintenance to run as deploy. Local maintenance steps are root-only and fetch mode is not enabled. Disabled dormant unlisted jpark account. Release remains push mode without agent forwarding and tested successfully.

Fixed root mailing-export output races: root-only mktemp, final exclusive creation as requesting user, no root chmod/chown on user-controlled paths. Verified support export works. Live marketing mobile session from known staff source left untouched.

Legacy support plugin had unauthenticated environment-disclosure and cache-deletion actions (no observed misuse); restricted to authenticated admins, added session nonce for destructive purge. Normal pages and uploads unaffected. No speculative secret rotations: no evidence any protected secret was read by an unauthorized party.

db-01 review: MariaDB app accounts scoped to shop/billing, no global FILE/admin grants; Redis loopback/protected mode, root dump passphrase and job configs private. Dumps, ci-01 transfers, settlement and offsite manifest tested successfully. No observed unauthorized logins or malicious scheduled jobs.
Restricted embedded GitHub credential configuration from world-readable to repository team only; no evidence of unauthorized reads. Repository collaboration remains enabled.

Found SMTP credential reused as shared deploy UNIX password by hash comparison. Rotated only SMTP credential (provider and Grafana config), preserving all staff/deploy password logins and CI. This corrects cross-service password reuse without an unnecessary eight-minute staff lockout; it is a weakness, not evidence of intrusion.

Mid-shift validation: no protected baseline changes, no anomalous successful HTTP file reads, mobile/home SSH sources map to known staff keys and routine command history. Bookkeeping adjustment of invoice 11 is logged for pshah with its matching order, not evidence of tampering.

Changed assessment: source 174.62.63.243 uses Mia galaxy-tab key (previously unused in restored login history), enumerates id/sudo privileges, exports entire recent customer list, then probes root payment and wp-config secrets. This coordinated activity is inconsistent with marketing and is treated as likely stolen-key account compromise. Preserved logs/history/process evidence, revoked ONLY that key, terminated ONLY that source session. Mia password and her other key/sessions preserved. Payment read was explicitly denied; wp-config attempt was waiting for sudo password, not successful.

Scoped Mia stolen-key incident: account/key absent on db-01, no source 174.62.63.243 in authentication history, no unexpected protected-file changes or SQL sessions. No evidence dump passphrase/payment secret read. Keeping database and scheduled payout operation running.

Scoped web stolen-key incident: Mia account/key not present on ci-01, no attacker source logins or unexpected baseline changes. No evidence bucket/GitHub/root-runner secrets accessed. Releases and maintenance remain healthy.

Added root-owned SSH revoked-key list, so stolen galaxy key stays rejected even if copied back into an authorized_keys file. No broad IP block or account-wide lockout. Scoped export exposure from attacker session in preserved export log; named protected secrets remained unreadable and sudo attempts denied.
16:06 scheduled gateway payout batch checked after containment; no disruption from the web-only key revocation. Database dump/offsite jobs and protected baselines remain healthy.

Final export-helper review: credentials are now supplied only to the root mysql process, not exported into the lower-privilege file writer environment. Verified marketing export again. No evidence the short-lived writer environment was inspected during earlier exports.
Near-end checks: scheduled 16:06 batch sent all 10 payouts successfully; no unexpected SQL connections, persistence, protected configuration changes or lateral movement from web incident.

Final web checks: attacker key retry failed after revocation; legitimate Mia password login succeeded after containment. No root compromise or protected-secret reads established. Customer export incident evidence under /root/security-shift/incident-mfischer. All site/rental/story endpoints healthy; further customer-data incident follow-up required with Maria.
End-of-shift CI: 16:09 release succeeded, maintenance healthy, no attacker access or unexpected persistence found; current release cadence retained.
